name: Cinnamon
short: Most reported adverse events are gastrointestinal upset and allergic reactions. Its coumarin can harm the liver; one case report describes hepatitis when taken with a statin.
text: A systematic review of adverse events (38 clinical trials, 20 case reports, 7 case series and spontaneous reports covering 160 events) found that the most frequent were gastrointestinal disorders and allergic reactions, self-limiting in most cases, and concluded that medicinal use at larger doses or for longer may be associated with significant adverse effects. An umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomised trials found no significant difference in toxic or side effects between cinnamon and placebo. Cinnamon contains coumarin, which can cause liver toxicity; a single case report describes hepatitis in a 73-year-old woman about a week after she added cinnamon supplements to long-term statin treatment, and its authors advised against combining cinnamon supplements with statins or other medicines that can harm the liver.
